newsitem.title: COLOMBIA: SOCCER-COLOMBIA SUFFER SHOCK DEFEAT AGAINST PERU.
newsitem.headline: SOCCER-COLOMBIA SUFFER SHOCK DEFEAT AGAINST PERU.

text.p: Colombia suffered a shock 1-0 defeat at home to Peru on Wednesday, their third successive loss in the South American World Cup qualifying competition.

It was also their second consecutive defeat in the Metropolitano stadium in Barraquilla, where they had believed themselves to be invincible, and the second time in three games they had failed to score.
Jose Pereda scored the winner with a spectacular long- distance shot to keep Peru well in the hunt for a place in France next year.

Colombia goalkeeper Farid Mondragon, blamed for the goals which allowed Argentina and Paraguay to beat Colombia in the last two games, was again at fault, throwing the ball straight to the Peruvian striker.

Colombia's place in France appeared a formality as they took a runaway lead in the nine-team group last year but they are now six points behind leaders Paraguay and only one ahead of third- placed Argentina.
Worse still, with 17 points from 10 games, they are in danger of being caught by the chasing pack of Bolivia, Ecuador, Peru and Uruguay, who all have 13 points. The top four teams qualify.
Colombia, with striker Faustino Asprilla serving the first of a two-game suspension, were rarely allowed to settle by Peru and went to pieces after falling behind in the 61st minute.
They were jeered off the pitch by the 30,000 crowd who towards the end of the game chanted "Ole" as the Peruvians passed the ball around.
